clue.text: At first, clubs always pursue several international players

indicators.note: 'at first' asks for the opening letter of each word that follows it

parts.note: first letter of clubs
first letter of always
first letter of pursue
first letter of several

explanation.surface: Football clubs are forever chasing a handful of star internationals.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a sentence about transfer targets, but its first four words only supply their initials.
explanation.definitionFit: A cap is awarded for each appearance for a national team, so capped players are called caps.

clue.text: Gallery supporting excellent film

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed underneath, so the first item sits below the second

parts.note: ace means first-rate
the Tate is a famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: A gallery is backing a superb movie.
explanation.walkthrough: TATE is London's Tate gallery; in a down answer it supports ACE by sitting below it.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetate is a transparent plastic sheet, a kind of film used in photography and overhead projection.

clue.text: Head of state is not, in short, a good person

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of state
ain't is the informal contraction of is not

explanation.surface: A cynical remark that a head of state is not, to put it briefly, a virtuous figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In short' points to the colloquial contraction ain't.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint is used loosely for anyone exceptionally kind or virtuous.

clue.text: Outlook in respect of English performers

parts.note: for can mean concerning or with regard to
standard abbreviation for English
the cast is the set of performers in a show

explanation.surface: A view of prospects concerning English actors.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlook is a prediction of what is to come, as in a weather forecast.

clue.text: Opponent fooled on odd occasions

indicators.note: odd occasions means the first, third and fifth positions are the ones kept

parts.note: the odd-numbered letters of fooled

explanation.surface: An adversary who was taken in now and again.
explanation.definitionFit: A foe is an enemy or adversary, a direct synonym of opponent.

clue.text: Reason to give people only some beer

parts.note: to ration is to allow people only a limited share
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A justification for handing out only part of the beer supply.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the underlying logic or justification for something.

clue.text: Patrol boats, say, protected by cannons at each side

indicators.note: something protected by another is enclosed by it on both flanks
the sides of a word are its two ends, so only its outer letters are kept

parts.note: the outermost letters of cannons
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: Coastal vessels flanked by guns on both sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for example' introducing the boats, but it is a verb to be put in the third person.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutter is a small fast vessel used by coastguards and customs for patrolling.

clue.text: When upset, young boy gets health food

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a lad is a young boy

explanation.surface: A sulky youngster is given something healthy to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A salad of raw vegetables is the stock example of wholesome eating.

clue.text: One occupying leadership position being stripped of power

indicators.note: stripped of means having something taken away, here a single letter

parts.note: a president holds the top post
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: A leader is losing their authority while still in office.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident is someone who lives in, or occupies, a place.

clue.text: Story of dog read out

indicators.note: reading out means speaking the word, so only its sound counts

parts.note: a dog has a tail, and to dog is also to tail someone

explanation.surface: Someone reads aloud a story about a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A tale is a narrative or story.

clue.text: A bit crazy, and it could be a can of worms!

definitions.text: it could be a can of worms

indicators.note: crazy means disordered, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something slightly mad that might turn out to be a messy problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A can of worms' is an idiom for a troublesome situation, but here it is taken literally, as an angler's supply.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglers use worms as bait, so a tin of them could literally be a fishing lure.

clue.text: Money coming from specialist yields, we're told

parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it, so the sound is what matters

parts.note: to cede is to yield or give up

explanation.surface: Cash generated by an expert's harvests.
explanation.definitionFit: Proceeds are the income earned from a sale or event.

clue.text: Bit of Mexican meal? One bit cooked in pot

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so the letters are mixed up
in places one thing inside another

parts.note: a pan is a cooking pot
the letters of one bit, scrambled

explanation.surface: A morsel of a Mexican dish, a single piece stewed in a pot.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows the definition is by example: one ingredient of a Mexican dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinto beans are speckled beans used widely in Mexican cooking, for instance in refried beans.

clue.text: Very short tailless mini rodents?

indicators.note: a short version of a word is missing its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before being cut

indicators.note: without a tail means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: taken as written before being cut

explanation.surface: Little tailless mice, asks the setter?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks rodents as an example of vermin rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Rats and mice are classic pests, the commonest creatures called vermin.

clue.text: Traveller settling finally in Antrim, possibly

indicators.note: in places one letter inside the rest
possibly suggests the place name is one of several arrangements
finally points to the last letter of the preceding word

parts.note: last letter of settling
the letters of Antrim rearranged

explanation.surface: A newcomer who has eventually settled in County Antrim, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: Antrim is a county in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A migrant is a person who moves from one place to another, a traveller.

clue.text: A school bringing in second uniform in a particular capacity

indicators.note: bringing something in means taking it inside

parts.note: taken as written
SCH is the abbreviation for school
S is the abbreviation for second
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A school is introducing an alternative uniform for a specific role.
explanation.definitionFit: As such means in that capacity or by its own nature, as in 'the leader as such'.

clue.text: Extensive evidence of debt hidden by police officers

indicators.note: something hidden by another is covered by it, so it sits inside

parts.note: cops are police officers
an IOU is a written acknowledgement of a debt

explanation.surface: Plenty of proof of money owed is being concealed by the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Copious means plentiful or abundant, covering a large amount.

clue.text: Noting changes in extremely recognisable call signal

indicators.note: changes means the letters are altered in order
in places one set of letters inside another
extremely means at the extremes, so only the end letters are kept

parts.note: outer letters of recognisable
the letters of noting rearranged

explanation.surface: Noticing alterations in a very familiar call sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringtone is the sound a phone makes to signal an incoming call.

clue.text: Best conceivable: one business arrangement

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a deal is a commercial agreement

explanation.surface: A single business agreement is described as the best possible.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal means perfect, the best that could be imagined.

clue.text: Intense enthusiasm of some pushy people

indicators.note: some means only a portion of the following words is taken

parts.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: Overbearing people show a great deal of zeal.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the end of pushy and the start of people.
explanation.definitionFit: Hype is excited, often exaggerated, enthusiasm or promotion.

clue.text: Expedition fails finally in dreadful heat

indicators.note: in places one letter inside the others
dreadful suggests something badly mangled, so the letters are jumbled
finally picks out the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: last letter of fails
the letters of heat rearranged

explanation.surface: A trek eventually collapses in terrible heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expedition' suggests a journey, but here it means speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Expedition can mean promptness or speed of action, the same sense as haste.

clue.text: Chance a version for testing

parts.note: to chance is to take a bet or gamble
taken as written

explanation.surface: Taking a gamble on a trial version of software.
explanation.definitionFit: In software, the beta is the near-final release given to users for trials before launch.

clue.text: European operation creating release of CO2 maybe

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European
a mission is a military or organised operation

explanation.surface: A European project that ends up giving off carbon dioxide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' signals that CO2 is just one example of what might be released.
explanation.definitionFit: An emission is a discharge of gas into the air, such as carbon dioxide from engines.

clue.text: Whimsical, somewhat topsy-turvy belief

indicators.note: topsy-turvy means upside down, which in a down clue reads bottom to top
somewhat means only part of the preceding word is used

parts.note: letters inside whimsical, taken before being turned round

explanation.surface: A fanciful, rather muddled creed.
explanation.definitionFit: An ism is any distinctive doctrine or ideology, a belief system.

clue.text: A canister placed in choice metal

indicators.note: placed in means set inside something else

parts.note: a plum job is a choice one
taken as written
a tin is a metal canister

explanation.surface: A container made from a top-quality metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Choice' is the adjective meaning select or desirable, as in a plum role.
explanation.definitionFit: Platinum is a precious metallic element.

clue.text: Each time at the end, the cha-cha is really simple

indicators.note: taking each word at its end means keeping every final letter

parts.note: last letter of the
last letter of cha-cha
last letter of is
last letter of really

explanation.surface: A dancer finds the cha-cha straightforward every time it finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Each' wants to be EA; instead the whole phrase tells you to take the last letter of each following word.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy means requiring little effort, the same as straightforward or simple.
